answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a probation ladder: a new identity starts at the wharf with zero trust and must complete small, verifiable jobs before it can handle valuable ones. Each completed job adds reputation, but a single proven fraud wipes the record and forfeits escrowed earnings, so spinning up a tide of fresh fake identities buys nothing — every sockpuppet must redo the slow climb. The cost is time and forfeited deposits, and the ripple effect is that honest agents accumulate a history no attacker can cheaply counterfeit.
